```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
dseams::dseams_threads(1L)
```

`dseams` reads one trajectory frame into the d-SEAMS engine and returns
data frames. A frame is one configuration. The analyses below take that
frame.

```{r}
library(dseams)
dseams_example()
```

`ice1h.lammpstrj` is a 2x2x2 ice Ih cell (128 oxygen sites).
`exampleTraj.lammpstrj` is one frame of a TIP4P mixture (250 waters;
type 2 is oxygen and type 1 is hydrogen). `nucleation_f1.lammpstrj` is
the first frame of an mW nucleation trajectory (4096 waters).

`type = 0` guesses oxygen. A positive type keeps that LAMMPS species. A
negative type keeps every atom.

## A perfect crystal

Keep every atom. This dump is oxygen only, so the frame has 128 rows.

```{r}
ice1h <- read_frame(dseams_example("ice1h.lammpstrj"), type = -1L)
ice1h
head(positions(ice1h))
```

Coordinates are in the units of the file, here angstrom. CHILL+ labels
every water hexagonal, and the hydrogen-bond network is six-membered
rings only. `graph = "cutoff"` bonds every pair closer than the cutoff
(3.5 angstrom). The default ring graph is the mutual four-neighbour
list, so the crystal census names `"cutoff"` explicitly.

```{r}
ice <- chill_plus(ice1h)
table(ice$name)
primitive_rings(ice1h, graph = "cutoff", max_depth = 6L)
cages(ice1h)
```

`name` is one of nine labels. `hexagonal` is ice Ih and `cubic` is ice
Ic. `interfacial` is ice-like but not cubic or hexagonal. `clathrate`
is clathrate and `interClathrate` is interfacial clathrate. `water` is
liquid or amorphous. `unclassified` matched none of those. `reCubic`
and `reHex` are cubic and hexagonal ice reclassified with the q6 order
parameter.

Cage membership is disjoint: hexagonal only, cubic only, both, or
water. On this cell every oxygen is in a hexagonal cage.

`symmetry()` compares each neighbour shell with ideal ice. The code is
0 for ice Ih, 1 for ice Ic, 2 for stacking-disordered ice, and -1
otherwise. On this cell every oxygen is code 0.

```{r}
table(symmetry(ice1h))
summary(steinhardt(ice1h, order_l = 6L)$ql)
```

`ql` is the local Steinhardt parameter. `qlbar` is the Lechner-Dellago
average of the same degree over the neighbour shell.

## A mixed frame

Type 2 is the oxygen in `exampleTraj.lammpstrj`.

```{r}
frame <- read_frame(dseams_example("exampleTraj.lammpstrj"), type = 2L)
frame
ice <- chill_plus(frame)
table(ice$name)
table(chill_plus(frame, graph = "mutual")$name)
```

`graph = "cutoff"`, the default for `chill_plus()`, is the distance
list: 9 interfacial clathrate and 241 water. `graph = "mutual"` keeps
the mutual four nearest neighbours inside the cutoff plus 1.5 angstrom:
1 clathrate, 7 interfacial clathrate, and 242 water.

`print()` on a CHILL+ result counts the labels. It does not print the
rows. Select the columns into a plain data frame when you want the
atoms:

```{r}
kept <- ice[ice$name != "water", ]
data.frame(atom = kept$atom, label = kept$label, name = kept$name)
```

The ring census and the order parameters are data frames in the same
way. The default ring graph is the mutual list. At depth 6 this frame
has 224 six-membered rings.

```{r}
primitive_rings(frame, max_depth = 6L)
q3 <- steinhardt(frame, order_l = 3L)
summary(q3$ql)
head(q4_q6(frame))
```

`q4_q6()` returns both degrees, and their neighbour averages `q4bar`
and `q6bar`, on the cutoff shell. `signature_cages()` counts closed
cages of one ring census. `"512"` is twelve pentagons, the small cage
of structure I. The two numbers are the cage count and the number of
atoms in those cages.

```{r}
signature_cages(frame, "512")
cages(frame)
```

## Rotation between two frames

`jump_tau90()` returns the time step `dt` when any water's H-H vector
rotates by at least 90 degrees between two frames, and `NaN` when none
does. Both frames must contain oxygen and hydrogen. In
`exampleTraj.lammpstrj` those species are types 2 and 1. The same frame
compared with itself has not rotated:

```{r}
both <- read_frame(dseams_example("exampleTraj.lammpstrj"), type = -1L)
jump_tau90(both, both, dt = 1, oxygen_type = 2L, hydrogen_type = 1L)
```
